:::{#def-natural-log}
#### Natural logarithm

For a real number $a > 0$,
the **natural logarithm** of $a$, written $\logf{a}$,
is the real number $y$ with $\expf{y} = a$.
The exponential function takes each positive value at exactly one input,
so there is exactly one such $y$,
and $\log : (0, \infty) \to \reals$ is the
[inverse function](sets-functions.qmd#def-inverse-function)
of $\exp$ (@def-exponential-function).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-log-notation}
#### Other notations for the natural logarithm

In these notes, $\logf{x}$ is always the natural logarithm,
the logarithm with base $e$ (@def-euler-number).
Some sources write $\ln x$ for the natural logarithm
and reserve $\log x$ for the logarithm with base 10.

:::
